plots.name: Execution cost
plots.caption: Figure 2 · Execution cost versus maximum devices per MEC server. Lower is better.
plots.insight: Load distribution lowers the proposed scheme’s cost relative to NLD. The gap is most pronounced at intermediate load: light load leaves little need to redistribute, while very high load leaves little spare capacity across servers.

plots.name: User satisfaction
plots.caption: Figure 3 · Fraction of tasks completed within delay tolerance. Higher is better.
plots.insight: Sharing spare server capacity helps maintain deadline satisfaction as device counts rise. Always-local and always-remote execution cannot adapt to resource availability on both sides.

plots.name: Nearby-server energy
plots.caption: Figure 4 · Energy consumed by nearby servers for tasks redistributed from MEC Server 1.
plots.insight: Compared with aggressive load distribution (ALD), the local-server-first policy moves fewer tasks to nearby servers and consumes less energy there. This is a specific redistributed-work metric, not total system energy.

stages.name: Classify & allocate radio
stages.text: At each server, classify devices into the paper’s S_mec and S_other sets, determine task priorities, and assign channels to S_mec devices in ascending priority order. Offloading needs both radio access and computation resources.

stages.name: Use the local MEC server
stages.text: Request the minimum compute rate Δ = d / (Tmax − Ttx). Allocate resources at the serving MEC server in ascending order of deadline until tasks are served or residual capacity is insufficient.

stages.name: Redistribute & split
stages.text: Try full distribution of unserved tasks to nearby servers before partial distribution. Choose a server with the smallest residual capacity that is strictly greater than the requested rate. If no single server fits, split into independent instructions, allowing time for the final gather instruction; terminate a task if instructions remain unserved.

stages.name: Revisit optional offloading
stages.text: For S_other devices, evaluate whether offloading reduces execution cost, assign channels to those that offload, and allocate computation resources to the tasks assigned to each server.
